item.text:
It’s understandable to want an explanation after reaching the final three and having two interviews—especially when your credentials appear stronger on some of the stated measures.

**An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence of bias or discrimination.** It is a fact about the panel’s composition, not proof of how its members assessed candidates. The same would be true of an all-men panel. Some universities have rules about panel composition, though, so checking the relevant policy is reasonable.

Your completed PhD, publications and teaching experience warrant a substantive explanation of the outcome, but they don’t establish that you were the strongest candidate overall. Publication quality and relevance, teaching assessments, disciplinary fit and industry experience may legitimately matter. The announcement may also omit qualifications. Crucially, check whether a completed PhD was **required**, and whether that requirement applied at application or by the start date.

I would focus first on the **criteria and process**, rather than the panel’s gender:

- Keep the advertisement, selection criteria, announcement and correspondence.
- Follow up now on your request, asking for the assessment of your application against the criteria and whatever comparative explanation can lawfully be shared.
- Check the university’s recruitment and review policies, including panel-composition requirements.
- Check complaint deadlines promptly; waiting for a response may not extend them.

You could write:

> I’m following up on my request of [date]. Please confirm when I can expect a written explanation of the selection decision, including how my application was assessed against the advertised criteria. Please also advise me of any review procedure and applicable deadlines.

More meaningful warning signs would be sex-based comments, inconsistent application of requirements, departures from recruitment rules, or an explanation that contradicts the documented criteria. **The panel’s composition and the two-week silence alone don’t establish any of those.**

Which country is the university in? That will determine your rights to reasons, records and review.
